newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle backs Guatemala boss in drugs case.
newsitem.headline: Nestle backs Guatemala boss in drugs case.

text.p: Food and beverage giant Nestle SA said on Thursday it had no reason to doubt the integrity of a Swiss local manager arrested in Guatemala in connection with an alleged drug smuggling ring.

Guatemalan national police on Wednesday said Andreas Haenggi would be charged with being part of a ring smuggling cocaine and heroin to Europe that allegedly also included his son, two German businessmen in Guatemala and the Antigua chief of police.
"Nestle has no reason to doubt the integrity of Mr Haenggi," a spokesman at Nestle global headquarters in Vevey, Switzerland, told reporters.
"Nestle will put all its resources at Mr Haenggi's disposal in order to help him with this difficult situation," he said.
Nestle said Haenggi, aged 60, has been head of its foodstuffs factory in the city of Antigua, Guatemala, since 1993 and had worked for the company for 20 years.
Haenggi was arrested in Antigua, Guatemala, a day after his 22-year-old son, Nicoloas Haenggi, was first taken in.
In Guatemala, police said they had detained the two Swiss as well as the interim police chief of the city of Antigua, Jose Luis Sebadua Salazar. All three were jailed pending formal charges.
Two Germans with a plant export business in Guatemala, Hartmut Zersch and Dieter Chomsi, were arrested in Germany as they returned from the Central American country.
"They were all linked to the same case. The charges are drug trafficking," National Police spokesman Francisco Villagran told reporters.
Carlos Giron, director of Guatemala's National Guard, said that the plant export company of the two Germans in Antigua was allegedly used as a cover-up to move drugs.
Giron said there may be more arrests in the case.
